question: According to the Python quick reference notes, what does PEP 8 recommend for indentation and naming?
answer: PEP 8 recommends four spaces per indentation level [S1] and snake_case for functions and variables [S1].

citations.title: Python Reference Notes
citations.text:
STYLE
PEP 8 recommends four spaces per indentation level, snake_case for functions and variables, CapWords for class names, and lines under 79 characters.

S2.title: Python Lecture Notes
S2.text: 2. Conditionals and Loops Conditionals use if, elif and else. Python uses indentation, normally four spaces, to define blocks; there are no braces. Only the first branch whose condition is true runs. Comparison operators are ==, !=, <, >, <= and >=; logical operators are and, or and not. Values such as 0, 0.0, "", [] and None are falsy; almost everything else is truthy. A for loop iterates over any iterable: for ch in "abc" visits each character, and for i in range(5) visits 0, 1, 2, 3, 4. range(start, stop, step) never includes stop. A while loop repeats as long as its condition is true, so the loop body must change something that eventually makes the condition false; otherwise you create an infinite loop. break leaves the nearest loop immediately. continue skips to the next iteration. A loop can have an else clause that runs only when the loop finished without hitting break.
